lucy: quick question  my country has a public holiday on Dec 26 but company shutdown is Dec 24Dec 31. can i swap that public holiday for a different day later, or do i have to take PTO?

jess (People Ops): good Q. if a national/public holiday falls inside the company shutdown we treat it as an observed company holiday (no PTO used). if your local holiday is outside the shutdown window and you want an alternate day, you can request a holiday swap. policy below. :flag-hooray:

omar (manager): lucy fyi we approved holiday swaps last year for a couple folks. managers need to confirm coverage before approving.

jess (People Ops): policy summary:
- public holidays observed by the company inside the shutdown = no PTO deduction.
- if your country has an extra statutory holiday that is NOT an observed company holiday, you may request a swap (1:1) to a different workday that quarter.
- swaps must be requested at least 14 days in advance and approved by your manager. people-ops finalizes cross-border exceptions.

lucy: perfect. second Q: if i get sick during the shutdown, does that count as sick leave or PTO?

nate (HR): sick during official company shutdown = treat as sick leave if you submit a sick note within 5 business days. we won't deduct PTO for verified sick time. if you can't get documentation (e.g., same-day urgent care closed) DM us and we'll work it out case-by-case.

lucy: nice. and what about half-days? some folks want to take half the week off for travel and work half-days. is that supported during blackout?

jess (People Ops): yes, half-day PTO is allowed but managers must verify coverage. during the company-wide blackout managers should minimize fractional approvals that complicate rotations. small teams should coordinate via the temporary-coverage channel.

omar (manager): to add: for small teams (<=6) we typically limit to 1 half-day off per person during the shutdown window unless we get cross-team coverage. please ping me if you need an exception.

jess (People Ops): also note carryover rules: our standard carryover cap is 40 hours. any balance above 40 at the cutoff is forfeited unless an exception is filed by Jan 31. swaps do not affect carryover calculations.

lucy: if someone is out on short-term disability and misses the cutoff, can we request a carryover exception?

nate (HR): yes, STD/medical exceptions are normally granted. manager should include medical documentation and proposed carryover amount when submitting. people-ops/HR coordinate on these. deadline still Jan 31 but we'll accept late medical exceptions with valid paperwork.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: "Holiday swaps must be filed 14 days prior. Carryover exception requests due Jan 31." <https://hr.redwood.com/holiday-swap>

jess (People Ops): last helpful bit  if you want a template for a swap request use: 

```
Swap request: Holiday swap (country-specific)
Employee: <name>
Local holiday date: YYYY-MM-DD
Requested swap date: YYYY-MM-DD
Manager approval: <manager name>
Reason: <brief reason>
```

jess (People Ops): i'll post a short FAQ and the swap form link in #announcements and pin it. thanks all :)

lucy: thanks everyone :sparkles:

people-ops-bot: Policy snippet: "Sick during shutdown: submit documentation within 5 business days to avoid PTO deduction."
